title: Guard each unit against misconceptions
statement: List the misconceptions each unit must guard against, and screen every text carrying a subject's content for them, even outside that subject's course, by meaning as well as phrase.
example: A later full-course evaluation counted 22 hits on its list of banned misconception phrasings across 8 lessons.
detail: A review of the reading course asked for unit-level misconceptions to guard against alongside each unit spine, including science misconceptions. The routing contract built from that review applies the misconception-check process to every science-bearing reading or writing text and asks that observation, hypothesis, theory, consensus, measurement, interpretation and opinion be distinguished accurately. A later full-course evaluation counted 22 Tier-1 misconception hits across 8 lessons. Simplify only where the text stays accurate and blocks no later learning.
against: there was no settled consensus science curriculum to check against, so a draft science ledger could not establish canonical scope or treatment (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0149-draft-grade-5-science-ledger.qmd`). The same brainlift rates the risk of misconceptions from wording as low in social studies, so the check bears hardest on science (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/Brainlift social science and science coherence.md`).
